newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr keeps a tenuous grip on 76 cents.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr keeps a tenuous grip on 76 cents.

text.p: The Australian dollar kept a tenuous grip on 76 cents at the midsession as would-be interbank sellers shied away from testing exporter bids beneath there.

Volumes were too light, however, to say with any confidence that a bottom had formed and dealers doubted the U.S. investment houses which had sold so aggressively last week had given up on their downside hopes. The outlook was clouded by much talk of options positions, some of which were supposed to be expiring this week with strikes down at the year low of US$0.7550.
April building approvals rose a much as expected 3.6 percent but private housing showed encouraging growth of 11 percent.
By 12.30 pm (0230 GMT) the dollar was hovering at US$0.7603/08 after edging up from an early US$0.7599/04.

But that was dead in line with Friday's soft US$0.7604/09 close and far below the US$0.7680 level held before April's dangerously weak retail trade data had started the market thinking about yet another rate cut.

Interest differential had moved even further against the currency, and in favour of the U.S. dollar, and left most traders looking for a test of key US$0.7550 support short term. A break there would return it to ground not seen since February last year and risk a retracement all the way to 73 cents.
Immediate resistance was put at US$0.7615 with more important levels at US$0.7630 and US$0.7680.
On the crosses the currency snuck higher on the mark as the market pondered the implications of the left wing's victory in the French general election.

The main opposition Socialist party won most seats but will need the support of the Communists to govern, leaving analysts fearing the new government will seek a loosening in the tough criteria of European monetary union.
The risk of having the hard mark swapped for a soft single currency saw the German unit marked down across the board.
The local dollar firmed to 1.3025/37 marks from 1.2941/53 late Friday, while the U.S. currency climbed to 1.7137/47 makrs from 1.7010/15.
The safe haven attraction fo the dollar bloc also helped the A$ inch up to 88.46/56 yen from an early 88.02/12 but that was still off on Friday's late 88.67/77.
In trade weighted terms it was unchanged at 58.0.

Today's domestic data had few short term implications for monetary policy, and therefore for the dollar. Further out, analysts said the 3.6 percent rise in overall building approvals confirmed the housing sector was in a steady, if slow, recovery.
The 11 percent rise in approvals for private sector houses, long considered the best bellweather of market health, came on top of a 4.5 percent gain in March to give annual growth of 12.9 percent.

The figures were hardly indicative of a housing boom, however, and would certainly not deter the Reserve Bank from easing again should economic growth look falling short of levels needed to reduce unemployment.
The bank's board meets Tuesday to discuss policy but analysts seriously doubt it would move so soon after its last easing on May 23. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
